=== PAST LEARNINGS (from prior, independent episodes) ===
OPERATING PRINCIPLES (distilled from prior episodes in this run -- APPLY these now, don't just note them):
Keep doing:
  - Delegating the full train/validate/pickle pipeline to a subagent with an explicit, detailed spec (exclude leakage columns like grade/sub_grade/int_rate/installment, build model_def.py as a standalone class with self-contained feature prep, sanity-check via fresh-process reload) produced a clean, working deliverable with no errors.
  - Treating 'event' as a binary classification target (1=default, 0=censored) with xgboost binary:logistic and comparing against a logistic regression baseline is a simple, fast approach that clearly beat the baseline (0.67 vs 0.60 c-index) and is easy to verify.
  - Running an explicit sanity check (load pickle in fresh process, predict on val_features_only.parquet and holdout_features_only.parquet, check shape/NaN/Inf/range) caught no issues here and is a good practice to repeat since it would catch broken pickles or encoding bugs before submission.
Avoid repeating:
  - Only one modeling approach (plain binary:logistic XGBoost with default-ish hyperparameters, no tuning) and one baseline (plain logistic regression) were tried; no attempt at a proper survival objective (e.g. survival:cox using observed_time) or hyperparameter search was made, which may be leaving c-index on the table (~0.67 achieved).
  - Categorical encoding builds a fresh label map per column by iterating train uniques in arbitrary order and assigns -1 to unseen categories at inference, but this was never explicitly stress-tested against holdout rows with categories absent from train to confirm it doesn't degrade predictions for a meaningful fraction of rows.
  - The per-column loop building the output DataFrame (inserting columns one at a time via out[c]=...) triggers a pandas 'highly fragmented frame' warning, indicating inefficient code that could be slow on larger datasets; using pd.concat for column assembly would be more robust/performant for scaling up feature engineering.

Identify the single strongest prior approach and describe it now.

input.recommended_approach: Train an XGBoost binary classifier (objective='binary:logistic') treating the survival 'event' field as a binary label (1=default, 0=censored), using all available features except known leakage columns (grade, sub_grade, int_rate, installment). Encode categoricals via a per-column label map built from train uniques (mapping unseen/holdout categories to -1). Compare against a plain logistic regression baseline fit on the same features. Implement this as a self-contained model_def.py class that does its own feature prep (so it can be pickled and reloaded independently), and explicitly sanity-check the pickled model in a fresh process by loading it and running predict on val_features_only.parquet and holdout_features_only.parquet, checking output shape, and absence of NaN/Inf and reasonable score range.
input.rationale: Across prior independent episodes, this was the only approach that was concretely implemented end-to-end and validated: it produced a clean, error-free deliverable and achieved the best measured result (c-index ~0.67 vs ~0.60 for logistic regression baseline), with an explicit reload/sanity-check step confirming robustness. No other approach (e.g., survival:cox, hyperparameter tuning) was actually tried and validated in past episodes, so this is the strongest concrete, proven starting point, though there is noted room for improvement (trying a proper survival objective, tuning hyperparameters, and stress-testing categorical encoding on unseen categories).
